update.title: OT-02 die, dead and perish words: Ch 2 death part rebuilt, claims registered
update.strand: life and death (M25), OT-02 Q1 What is death?
update.researcher_instruction: "proceed with the weave as proposed, include the perish pull. What I am seeing is encouraging that we heading in right direction." (2026-10-14), on check v2; earlier: "check the completeness and validity of existing claims, check narration for unsubstantiated or unrecorded claims, and check the verses for perspectives that were missed in the first round"; "have you adequately recognised the different perspectives of death related to 'spiritual death', 'dead to sin', 'causes of death'"
update.method: Die/death words (H4191, H4194, G0599, G2288) checked against the claims and Ch 2 by unit-2 face; the dead/die words hidden in T-codes (G3498 and 16 others, 250 verses) and the perish words (H0006, G0622, G0684, 271 verses) pulled and read. Ch 2 death part rebuilt by kind of death (Death spoken of in more than one way; Death in the living with stated causes and the way out; new Dead to sin; new Those left behind); 10 statements corrected (OT-02.10 counts); 31 + 16 claims registered with tellings. Pointers in 10.10, 10.12 (working note removed), 12 and 14.
update.structure_change: Ch 2: new subsections "Death spoken of in more than one way" and "Dead to sin" under What death is; new section "Those left behind" before Wanting to die
update.structure_reason: The death words were read by face, not by which death; the kinds, the dead-in/dead-to change and the stated causes had no one account; Ch 2 had no place for death as the living meet it in another
update.quote_note: the 8 non-matches are section names in quotation marks, not Scripture

new.text: Life is held in the breath, and the breath is God's to give and to take back
new.beyond_text: gathers the verses of God and the breath

new.text: When the breath goes, a person's plans go with it
new.beyond_text: reads "plans perish" as the thinking going with the breath

new.text: God holds both ends, killing and making alive, and keeps alive between them
new.beyond_text: joins the "I kill and I make alive" sayings with the keeping alive

new.text: The breath also gives understanding, and words come out on it
new.beyond_text: joins the understanding and the speaking verses of the breath

new.text: The breath can fail in someone still alive
new.beyond_text: sets two verses as one statement

new.text: God gives human frailty as a reason for holding back his anger
new.beyond_text: joins Isaiah 57 and Psalm 78

new.text: Humans and animals share one breath and one lot
new.beyond_text: gathers the verses

new.text: Life and death are set before a person to choose; life is chosen by doing, seeking and holding on
new.beyond_text: gathers the commands that end "and live"

new.text: Long days are promised with some commands, and the Preacher sets the righteous who perish beside them; both are stated
new.beyond_text: sets the promise and the Preacher side by side

new.text: Wisdom marks where the way to death ends, and some of what kills a person is named from within
new.beyond_text: gathers the wisdom sayings on the way to death

new.text: God has no pleasure in anyone's death and calls for turning; the turning is a considered act that reaches back over the past, and trust can lean the wrong way
new.beyond_text: joins Ezekiel 18 and 33

new.text: Life can be wrongly kept or taken by lying words
new.beyond_text: reads Ezekiel 13:19 as a general statement

new.text: The same message is death to one and life to another
new.beyond_text: states what 2 Corinthians 2:16 shows of how one thing changes character

new.text: Another's death can be laid at a person's hand
new.beyond_text: reads the watchman as a general case

new.text: The commonest form of the oath by life is "As the Lord lives" (39 verses); in six of them a second life is joined
new.beyond_text: a count over the oath verses (2026-10-14)

new.text: The oath "As the Lord lives" places a promise before the living God and binds the speaker to it by life
new.beyond_text: reads what the oath does

new.text: The oath's words stay the same while the heart that speaks them differs; it is judged by how it is sworn
new.beyond_text: sets several oaths side by side

new.text: God swears by his own life, and the oath carries what he wants and what he will do
new.beyond_text: gathers the "As I live" oaths

new.text: "The living God" sets him against idols, which have no breath
new.beyond_text: joins the name with Habakkuk 2

new.text: The inner being turns toward the living God, or away from him
new.beyond_text: gathers four verses

new.text: Scripture counts a life in days and says what the days are for
new.beyond_text: gathers the "all the days" verses

new.text: The world where life is lived is named "the land of the living"
new.beyond_text: gathers the phrase

new.text: People weigh their own lives: loathed, worn down, enjoyed, and not consisting in possessions
new.beyond_text: gathers the verses that weigh a life

new.text: Where the hope of seeing good has gone, life is weighed as a breath
new.beyond_text: joins Psalm 34:12 and Job 7:7

new.text: The difference in how a life is weighed lies in what each verse sets life beside
new.beyond_text: reads the verses of Life weighed together

new.text: Death's certainty can be turned into a reason to indulge, and Scripture answers it
new.beyond_text: joins Isaiah 22 and 1 Corinthians 15

new.text: The law weighs a life by what it has begun, and names what a death can leave unfinished
new.beyond_text: reads Deuteronomy 20:5-7

new.text: What lies beyond death is not shown to a person
new.beyond_text: states the point of God's question to Job

new.text: Scripture speaks of death in more than one way: the body's death, death in the living, dying to sin, a death beyond death, death as a power, and the living made like the dead
new.beyond_text: sets the uses of the death words side by side (OT-02 check v2 section G)

new.text: The father sets "dead" beside "lost" and "alive" beside "found"; to perish and to be lost are one word
new.beyond_text: joins Luke 15 with the perish verses

new.text: "Dead in" trespasses and "died to" sin are opposites: death under sin, and death that ends its rule
new.beyond_text: sets Ephesians 2 and Colossians 2 beside Romans 6 and 7 (3 and 6 verses)

new.text: The word "dead" passes to sin itself, to faith and to works
new.beyond_text: gathers the uses

new.text: Some are perishing now, set against being saved; what is set against perishing is eternal life
new.beyond_text: gathers the present perishing verses

new.text: Where a verse sets death against eternal life (Romans 6:23) it speaks of more than the body's death; other verses do not say which death, and are left as written
new.beyond_text: reads Romans 6:23 by its opposite

new.text: In Acts a lie contrived in the heart is followed at once by death, and fear comes on all who hear
new.beyond_text: joins Acts 5:3-11

new.text: Inner things can perish: hope, endurance, courage (the heart), wisdom and truth
new.beyond_text: gathers the perish verses said of inner things

new.text: The verses name what brings death in the living, each in its own place; no verse gathers them into one list
new.beyond_text: gathers the stated causes without joining them

new.text: The verses name the way out of death in the living: hearing the Son and believing, God making alive with forgiveness, waking, coming home; loving the brothers is its sign
new.beyond_text: gathers the way-out verses

new.text: One person's freedom can destroy another
new.beyond_text: joins 1 Corinthians 8 and Romans 14

new.text: The believer has already died to sin, to the law and to the powers of the world, and a putting to death is still to be done
new.beyond_text: gathers the dying-to verses

new.text: Kings and Chronicles tell the deaths of kings as sleeping with their fathers (36 verses)
new.beyond_text: a count of "slept with his fathers" (2026-10-14)

new.text: The coming of death is often met with anguish and terror, and the fear of dying shapes what people do
new.beyond_text: gathers the verses of the inner being under the coming of death

new.text: "The king of terrors" is Bildad's word, said of Job, and God's verdict on the friends stands over it
new.beyond_text: sets Job 18:14 under Job 42:7

new.text: The nearness of death is given a purpose: to rely on God who raises the dead
new.beyond_text: joins 2 Corinthians 1:9 and Hebrews 5:7

new.text: A death is met by those who remain: grief, not watching, fasting and then eating, reproach, limits on mourning, mourning withheld, and death not taken to heart
new.beyond_text: gathers the verses of those left behind

new.text: People sometimes want to die; of the 24 verses with such a wish, 17 name no inner word
new.beyond_text: a count over the wish-to-die verses (2026-10-14)

new.text: Of the seven wishes to die answered in these passages, two are fed, two are answered another way, and three are granted, each to a man already blinded or wounded
new.beyond_text: a count over the answered wishes

new.text: Giving life belongs to the Father, the Son and the Spirit
new.beyond_text: gathers four verses

new.text: The dead made alive are living people; the crossing from death to life happens now, and life is spoken of as had now and still to come
new.beyond_text: joins Paul and John

new.text: The making alive rests on a death, and Christ went to it himself
new.beyond_text: joins the verses of his death

new.text: That death changes how the living live: no longer for themselves, dead to sin, Christ living in them
new.beyond_text: joins Paul and Peter

new.text: A death, too, can belong to the Lord, and a dying can go on while a person lives
new.beyond_text: joins Romans 14 with Paul's own words

new.text: Scripture speaks of the death of the upright in its own words: precious, wished for, a refuge, in faith, bearing fruit, glorifying God
new.beyond_text: gathers the verses without making one a heading for the rest

new.text: Some wait to see one thing before they die, and then let go
new.beyond_text: joins Simeon and Jacob

new.text: People hold to someone, or to something, even to death, and the readiness can fail
new.beyond_text: gathers the verses of readiness to die

new.text: The living are told how to deal with the dead: inquiring of them and offering to them are forbidden; kindness to the dead is blessed
new.beyond_text: gathers the verses
